# Service Pack Release Dashboard — Linux/Podman Deployment Guide

This guide documents how to build, harden, ship, and operate the container
image for the shared Linux/Cockpit/Podman server, following the internal
per-port application platform model (host nginx owns public TLS termination;
the container publishes only to loopback; one public HTTPS port per app).

## Deliverables

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`Containerfile`](Containerfile) | Multi-stage build (Vite SPA build → slim `node:22-alpine` runtime) |
| [`.containerignore`](../.containerignore) / [`.dockerignore`](../.dockerignore) | Build-context exclusions (secrets, `.git`, dev tooling) — kept in sync |
| [`.env.example`](.env.example) | Application variable **names only** — no values |
| `.env` (next to the exported tar) | Runtime container paths for the shared workbook and PDF; transfer separately, never bake into the image |
| `README-deploy.md` | This file |
| `service-pack-release-dashboard.tar` | Exported image (`podman save`) — generate per Section 4; not committed to git |

The delivered `.env` contains only file paths. The image contains no `.env`,
TFS PAT, TLS private key, or corporate certificate.

## 1. What the image contains — and does not

Final runtime image contents (everything else is excluded by
`.containerignore`/multi-stage discard):

```
/app/server.js
/app/dist/                         (built SPA — public/ + Vite output)
/app/service-pack-planning.xlsx
/app/node_modules/                 (production dependencies only)
/app/package.json, package-lock.json
```

It does **not** contain: `.git`, `.env`, TypeScript/Vite/React build
tooling, root-owned npm cache/log remnants, or any Node compile cache
(`NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` is intentionally never set).

**Dependency classification fix:** `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom`,
and `typescript` are declared in `package.json` as `devDependencies` — they
are bundled into the static SPA by Vite during the build stage and are never
`require()`-d by `server.js`, so the production runtime install
(`npm ci --omit=dev`) no longer installs them. This is the actual fix for the
image bloat (95 vs. 114 production packages; ~6 MB vs. tens of MB of
node_modules) — reclassifying dependencies, not deleting files after the
fact, since the previous image already used a production-only install stage
but that install target incorrectly included frontend-only packages.

## 2. Removed / changed application behavior

The "Product list" tab (Windchill document sign-in modal and its supporting
routes) has been removed — it was a desktop-oriented, credential-gated
feature unrelated to this app's core purpose. Removed with it, since they
existed solely to support that tab:

- `POST /api/windchill-product-list`, `GET /api/open-windchill-doc`
  (spawned `xdg-open`/`start`/`open` to launch a local file browser — would
  never have worked in a headless Linux container anyway), and
  `GET /api/product-list` (read the server process's own `~/Downloads`
  folder — a container has no such folder).
- The `httpntlm` dependency and `WindchillModal` component (no longer
  reachable from any UI path).
- `WINDCHILL_*` environment variables (no longer read by the server).

**SP Guideline PDF** now follows the same live-source-with-fallback pattern
as the planning workbook (Section 3b): `GET /api/sp-guideline-pdf` reads from
`SP_GUIDELINE_PDF_PATH` when set, falling back to the bundled PDF in
`public/`.

**CORS** was `cors()` with no options (reflects any `Origin` header back with
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`). It is now an explicit allow-list via
`ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (comma-separated), defaulting to **no cross-origin access**
when unset — correct for this app, since the SPA and its API are always
served same-origin through host nginx. Only set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` if a
specific split-origin embedding scenario requires it.

## 3. Corporate CA handling (decision required before production use)

The image declares `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corporate-ca.crt`
but never bakes in a certificate (certificates rotate; baking one in would
require an image rebuild on every rotation). **Operator must choose one:**

- **(A) The Linux server's egress path intercepts TLS** (e.g. a corporate
  proxy/inspection appliance) — outbound `axios` calls to TFS/Azure DevOps
  will fail TLS validation without the CA. Obtain the public
  corporate root CA certificate from IT and mount it read-only:
  ```bash
  podman run -d --name spr-dashboard \
    -v /opt/spr-dashboard/corporate-ca.crt:/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corporate-ca.crt:ro \
    ...
  ```
  Never mount an empty/missing file — Podman will silently create it as an
  empty **directory**, which breaks Node's TLS trust store entirely.
- **(B) The server's egress path does not intercept TLS** — remove the
  `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` line from [`Containerfile`](Containerfile) (Node then
  uses the standard public CA bundle already installed via `ca-certificates`
  in the image).

This is unrelated to nginx's TLS certificate (Section 5) — that terminates
the browser-facing HTTPS connection; this CA is for the container's own
*outbound* HTTPS calls.

## 3b. Planning workbook source (network share vs. bundled snapshot)

The dashboard's Q1–Q4 charts and status tables read `service-pack-planning.xlsx`.
The authoritative source of truth is the internal file share:

```
\\ingbtcpic1vwsfs.code1.emi.philips.com\Bangalore3\Projects\DXR\FSA\Service pack planning sheet\service-pack-planning.xlsx
```

Set `SP_PLANNING_XLSX_PATH` to read from it instead of the bundled snapshot
committed in the repo. If unset, or if the configured path is temporarily
unreadable, the server falls back to the bundled copy and logs a warning
(`GET /api/service-pack-xlsx` also returns a `source` field —
`external` | `bundled` | `bundled-fallback` — so this is observable at runtime).

**A raw Windows UNC path only resolves in native Windows execution**
(`npm run server`, not containerized) — a Linux container's userspace
(including this image, and even a Linux container running on a Windows
Podman/WSL host) cannot resolve `\\server\share\...` syntax directly. For
any containerized deployment:

1. Mount the **Bangalore3 share** on the **host** via a CIFS/SMB client to a
   stable POSIX path (Linux host, requires `cifs-utils` and a host-owned
   credentials file with the domain service account, mode `0600`; confirm
   the server's supported SMB version with its administrator):
   ```bash
   sudo mkdir -p /mnt/bangalore3
   sudo mount -t cifs '//ingbtcpic1vwsfs.code1.emi.philips.com/Bangalore3' \
     /mnt/bangalore3 -o credentials=/etc/sp-planning-cifs-credentials,ro,vers=3.0
   ls -l '/mnt/bangalore3/Projects/DXR/FSA/Service pack planning sheet/service-pack-planning.xlsx' \
     '/mnt/bangalore3/Projects/DXR/FSA/Service pack planning sheet/2009001390 Service Pack Guideline_en 1.pdf'
   ```
   Confirm the container user can read both files; a successful ping does not
   establish SMB access or file permissions. The host administrator must
   arrange for the CIFS mount to persist across server restarts.
2. Bind-mount the share read-only into the container:
   ```bash
   -v /mnt/bangalore3:/mnt/bangalore3:ro
   ```
3. Point the app at the in-container paths in the runtime `.env`:
   ```
   SP_PLANNING_XLSX_PATH=/mnt/bangalore3/Projects/DXR/FSA/Service pack planning sheet/service-pack-planning.xlsx
   SP_GUIDELINE_PDF_PATH=/mnt/bangalore3/Projects/DXR/FSA/Service pack planning sheet/2009001390 Service Pack Guideline_en 1.pdf
   ```

Do not put the CIFS credentials file inside the image or the git repository.
Treat it as a host-owned secret, same class as the JFrog pull credential.

**SP Guideline PDF follows the identical pattern** via `SP_GUIDELINE_PDF_PATH`
(`GET /api/sp-guideline-pdf`), pointing at the same share:

```
\\ingbtcpic1vwsfs.code1.emi.philips.com\Bangalore3\Projects\DXR\FSA\Service pack planning sheet\2009001390 Service Pack Guideline_en 1.pdf
```

Since it's the same share, one CIFS mount and one container bind mount cover
both files. Do not set either path to a Windows UNC path in a Linux container.

**IB System Release Versions workbook** follows the same pattern via
`IB_SYSTEM_VERSIONS_XLSX_PATH` (`GET /api/ib-system-versions-xlsx`). It is
optional: if unset, the copy bundled in the image is shown. To read it live,
place the workbook on the Bangalore3 share (covered by the same mount) and
add the in-container path to the runtime `.env`, e.g.:

```
IB_SYSTEM_VERSIONS_XLSX_PATH=/mnt/bangalore3/Projects/DXR/FSA/Service pack planning sheet/IB System Release Versions.xlsx
```

## 4. Build, verify, and export the image

Run on the Linux Podman host (or transfer the resulting `.tar`):

```bash
git clone <repo-url> service-pack-release-dashboard
cd service-pack-release-dashboard

# Build in Docker image format so HEALTHCHECK is preserved
# (Podman defaults to OCI format, which silently drops HEALTHCHECK)
podman build --format docker -f docker/Containerfile -t service-pack-release-dashboard:1.3.0 .

# Confirm image contents and healthcheck are present
podman inspect service-pack-release-dashboard:1.3.0 | grep -A5 -i healthcheck
podman run --rm service-pack-release-dashboard:1.3.0 sh -c "du -sh /app/node_modules && ls /app"

# Export for transfer (only if not pushing to a registry — see build-push.ps1/.sh)
podman save --format docker-archive -o service-pack-release-dashboard-1.3.0.tar service-pack-release-dashboard:1.3.0
```

On the target machine: `podman load -i service-pack-release-dashboard-1.3.0.tar`.

## 5. Runtime deployment (rootless Podman + host nginx)

Example port chain for one application slot (illustrative — the platform
administrator assigns the real public/private ports; never hard-code them
into the image):

```
NGINX public :18087 (TLS)  →  Podman loopback :28087  →  container :8080
```

### 5.1 Runtime configuration (`.env`)

Copy the `.env` delivered alongside the image tar to the host (or populate
a copy of [`.env.example`](.env.example)). The delivered file contains only
the in-container planning/PDF paths shown in Section 3b. Add
`IB_SYSTEM_VERSIONS_XLSX_PATH` if using a live IB workbook instead of the bundled copy. Adjust the
paths if the administrator chooses a different container mount point.
Keep credentials out of this file; if adding TFS credentials later, protect
and distribute it as a secret. Install it outside git, readable only by
the account that runs Podman:

```bash
install -d -m 0700 /opt/spr-dashboard
install -m 0600 /path/to/transferred/.env /opt/spr-dashboard/.env
```

Run from the same account that owns the env file. Podman passes the file's
variables to the container via `--env-file` (do not bake it into the image).
The host mount must already exist and contain both files:

```bash
podman run -d --name spr-dashboard \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --publish 127.0.0.1:28087:8080 \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  --env-file /opt/spr-dashboard/.env \
  -v /mnt/bangalore3:/mnt/bangalore3:ro \
  localhost/service-pack-release-dashboard:1.3.0
```

If decision (A) in Section 3 applies, add its CA bind mount to this command.
If the container already exists, it must be recreated to change its env
file or bind mounts. Changing workbook/PDF contents in the mounted share
requires no new image; use **Refresh data** in the dashboard. Check
`GET /api/service-pack-xlsx` for `"source":"external"`; `"bundled-fallback"`
indicates the configured external workbook was not read.

### 5.2 Health check

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:28087/health
# Expected: {"status":"ok"}
```

`podman ps` should show the container as `healthy` after the
`HEALTHCHECK`'s `start-period` (10s) plus one interval (30s).

### 5.3 Host nginx (root-managed) reverse proxy

```nginx
server {
    listen 18087 ssl;
    listen [::]:18087 ssl;

    server_name <server-fqdn>;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/tls/<server-directory>/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/tls/<server-directory>/server.key;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:28087;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}
```

Run `nginx -t` then reload nginx as the platform administrator. This app has
no WebSocket/SSE traffic, so no `Upgrade`/`Connection` headers are needed.

## 6. Operations

```bash
podman logs --tail 200 spr-dashboard
podman restart spr-dashboard          # persistent state: none — no DB/volume to preserve
podman stop spr-dashboard && podman rm spr-dashboard
```

Upgrades: pull/load the new image tag, stop the old container, start a new
one with the same `--publish`/volume flags against the new tag. There is no
persistent database or volume for this application, so no backup/restore
step is required beyond the `.env` secret file itself.

## 7. Local smoke testing only (not production)

`docker/docker-compose.standalone.yml` builds and runs the same
[`Containerfile`](Containerfile) for local Podman Desktop verification.
Production deployment uses the rootless `podman run` commands in Section 5,
not Compose.
